full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman J : This First Miscellaneous appeal, at the instance of petitioner-appellant is directed against the judgment and order dated 21-1-2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong refusing to set aside the award dated 9-3-2006 passed by the Arbitral Tribunal thereby disallowed the Miscellaneous Case No. 160 of 2006. 

 5. After pronouncement of the award, 2ncl party before the District Judge, Chittagong on an application under section 42 read with section 43 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 sought for setting aside the award. The learned District Judge on the basis of the aforementioned application stared Miscellaneous Case No. 160 of 2006. Eventually, said Miscellaneous Case was transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong for hearing and disposal. Learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong after hearing the parties by his order dated 21-1-2007 refused to set aside the Arbitration award and thereby disallowed the Miscellaneous Case No. 160 of 2006 affirming the Arbitration award. 

 6. Hence, the 2nd party petitioner as appellant preferred the instant 1st Miscellaneous Appeal before this Court. 

 8. The learned Advocate clearly and specifically pointed out that the letter dated 25-7-05 sought for arbitration is not within the ambit of clause X of the contract agreement dated 18-10-2004, referring the above clause, he added. Therefore starting the arbitration proceeding is totally misconceived and award in question is beyond the agreement. He further submitted that the learned Arbitrators acted beyond the contract agreement in passing the award holding that in column 4 of financial offer form there is a bonafide mistake regarding number of boat thereby beyond the authority and jurisdiction directed the authority concern to correct the same. He further referring the award submitted that the learned Arbitrators also directed the 2nd party rectify and amend the existing contract dated 18-10-2004 by a supplementary contract agreement which are beyond the jurisdiction of the Arbitrators. He added that according to sub section (a) (VI) and, (b) III and (IV) of section 43 of the Arbitration Act 2001 the learned Arbitrators exceeded the jurisdiction and thereby acted beyond the scope of the submission to arbitration. Therefore, the award in question is illegal and same is liable to be set aside. He lastly submitted that the instant award is against the public policy of Bangladesh because after signing of contract and taking 50% advance of contract money if bidder sought for price escalation and unsuccessfully prayed for arbitration with direction for rectification of contract in violation of arbitration clause in the name of so called unilateral mistake the authority concern will be unable to implement the policy work with a heavy cost in violation of agreement which clearly goes against the public interest. In support of his submission he relied upon numbers of decisions, which are:" 

 9. The case of Associated Engineering Co vs Government of Andhra Pradesh reported in AIR (SC) 232, the case of Hyundai Corporation vs Sumikin in Bussan Corporation reported in 22 BLD (AD) 16 = 54 DLR (AD) 88, the case of State of Gujrat (Commissioner of Sales Tax, Ahmadabad) vs Varity Body Builders reported in AIR 1976 (SC) 2108, the case of Life Insurance Corporation of India vs Dharam VIR Anand reported in 7 SCC 348, the case of Olympus Super Stracture Pvt Ltd. vs Meena Vijoy Khetan reported in 5 Supreme Court Case 651 the case of Executive Engineer LGED, Rangpur vs A Latif & Company Ltd. reported in DLR 656, the case of Ananda Builders Ltd vs Bangladesh Water Transport Authority reported in 57 DLR (AD) 31. 

 10. Mr Moudud Ahmed, with Abul Kalam Patwary, Advocates, appearing for the respondent submitted that the appellant as 2nd party participated in the reference by appointing Arbitrator and also submitted the documents and contested in the reference before the arbitral tribunal and being aggrieved by the decision of the tribunal filed Miscellaneous Case before the learned District Judge, Chittagong for setting aside the award unsuccessfully filed the instant first Miscellaneous Appeal, thus the instant appeal is not sustainable in law. He submitted that learned Additional District Judge rightly refused to set aside the award as it was awarded in accordance with law. He further submitted that in reference the learned Arbitrators did not commit any misconduct or acted beyond jurisdiction, therefore, the learned Additional District Judge rightly found that there is no ground to set aside the award. He added that in the contract agreement there is a specific provision of Arbitration if any dispute arise among the parties, therefore, Arbitrators rightly enter into the reference and passed the award. He further added that the award passed by the learned Arbitral tribunal does not suffer from any legal infirmity as such no interference calls for by this Court. In support of this contentions he relied upon numbers of decisions which are:- 

 l1. The case of Bangladesh Power Development Board vs Arab Contractor (BD) reported in VI ADC 952, the case of Sudarsan Trading Co vs Government of Kerala reported in 1989 AIR (SC) 890, the case of Puri Construction Pvt Ltd vs Union of India reported in AIR 1989 (SC) 777, the case of Mssers Ihad & Co vs Province of Sind. reported in PLD 1980 Karachi 207, the case of KM Shaft Limited vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 1983 BCR (AD) 155, the case of Begum Khadiza Akter Banuvs AKM Amanullah reported in BCR 1985 (AD) 8, the case of Muhammad Shagir Bhatti and Sons vs Federation of Pakistan reported in 10 DLR (SC) 169. 

 16. In reference learned Arbitrators unanimously found that the 1st party respondent on a bonafide mistake in column 4 of the financial offer form annexure- "B" after word "quoted amount" 2(two) nos fast patrol complete boats" have been written in place of "for one complete boat which was affirmed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong disallowing the Miscellaneous case thereby refused to set aside the award. 

 19. Before discussing the merits of the case, we like to refer the case of Associated Engineering vs Government of Andhra Pradesh wherein following principles have been enunciated. 

 It has held by the Supreme Court of India in the case of Associated Engineering Co vs Government of Andhra Pradesh reported in 4 sec (1991) page 93 "A dispute as to jurisdiction error-Award beyond limits of the contract- Arbitrator cannot act arbitrarily, irrationally, capriciously or independent of the contract- Award deliberately departing from the contract, apart from constituting misconduct also constitutes mala fide action-Award made disregarding the contract goes to the root of jurisdiction of the Arbitrator. 

 (iii) The party making the application was not given proper notice of the appointment of an arbitrator or of the arbitral proceedings or was otherwise unable due to some reasonable causes to present his case. 

 (b) The Court or High Court Division, as the case may be, is satisfied that- 

 34. First party in his letter dated 25-7-2005 has stated the cause of action of dispute and sought for arbitration inter alia that due to ambiguity in column 4 of the financial offer form annexure-"B" in a pre-bid meeting it has been amended adding (for complete boat) after word "amount quoted" thus quotation has been desired for one complete boat or each boat or each unit because that phrase "for complete boat" denotes singular number. Thereafter, 1st party respondent company in fact ands indeed quoted the amount of Taka 17,42,26,000 only as a rate of one complete boat but due to mistake, written for 2(two) nos fast patrol boats instead of one complete boat in the column 4 of financial offer form. But from the prayer of statement of claim it appears that in fact first party prayed for direction to rectify the contract agreement in the name of mistake in column 4 of the financial offer form. Accordingly learned arbitrators directed the 2nd party to rectify the contract agreement dated 18-10-2004 and further directed to execute a supplementary argument for the second boat at the same consideration and on similar terms conditions which was not agreed and included in the arbitration clause of the agreement. From the above direction it appears that the arbitrators sit in the arbitration not for arbitrate the dispute in the term of agreement but as a higher authority over the parties in agreement. In the instant case, the arbitrators supersede the contract agreement and themselves out stepped the confines of the contract. Error arose not only by superseding the contract but was an error going to the roof of the jurisdiction of the arbitrators because the learned arbitrators asked the wrong action and awarded in excess of the authority. Learned arbitrators in awarding the claim deal with the dispute not contemplated by or not fallen within the terms of contract and beyond the scope of the submission of arbitration. 

 35. In the instant case it appears on the face of award that learned arbitrators seriously tried to interpret phrase "one complete boat" as a singular number allegedly used in column 4 of the financial offer form in a pre-bit meeting but quite silent about the plural phrases used in the contract agreement, in the heading of tender documents and in the heading of the financial offer form and another papers. It appears to us that learned arbitrators without considering the materials on record erroneously passed the award directing the 3nd party to change all plural words and phrases to a singular acting beyond the authority. 

 39. In the instant appeal it appears that the 2nd party Chittagong Port Authority floated the tender for consideration and delivery of 2(two) fast patrol boats in terms of tender document. 6(six) bidders including the first party participated in the bid. First party's offer became responsive. Contract agreement and work order was issued in favour of 1st party. Pursuant to contract agreement first party submitted the performance bond, thereafter 1st party took 50% advance of the contract price 2nd party CPA is an autonomous statutory body which operates Chittagong sea port of the country. CPA floated tender for construction and delivery of 2(two) Nos. of fast patrol boats for Bangladesh Coast Guard for security and patrolling the see area of Bangladesh from its own found i.e. from public found. Since question of financial interest of state is seriously involved in the instant case, Thus 2nd party in the policy making and functioning transparency is desired. Thus, the 2nd party must be in favour of public policy. 

 41. However, we have gone through the decisions as referred by learned counsel for the respondent, we are respectful agreement with the principles enunciated therein, but facts leading to those cases' are quite distinguishable to that of the instant case, therefore, we are unable to accept his submission.
